body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE. Scope: the currently authorized Coder/Merger workflow. This memory records operating guidance; recover the acting project's current STOP/resume and authority before execution.

1. The Merger is non-authoring. A Coder implements changes, runs the new/focused tests, freezes the input and obtains the required independent reviews. Focused tests are selected from the actual dependency impact as well as new behavior: when a change adds calls across component boundaries, include the existing applicable boundary/architecture guards before READY. A passing filtered subset does not cover an excluded affected guard; this adds no Coder-side full gate. The complete package identifies scope, base, patch/root and fingerprint, actual test outcomes, full review results and disposition of findings.
2. READY requires complete required independent reviews of the actual package changes, including changed tests and documentation. Read full results, coverage gaps and finding disposition; an unread in-scope gap is not a clean review. Each host-issued review attempt, including a supported follow-up in the same delegation, needs its own structured result before the final reply. 'Exactly once' applies per attempt, not per session lifetime. Missing/failed submission is unavailable, never a clean review; prose alone cannot replace it. The existing parent owns supported recovery; do not dispatch a duplicate review pair. Under Greg's current TermAl-model direction, those reviews finish before the complete READY handoff. The Merger may cleanly carry the unchanged reviewed package onto current master and run the required gate on the exact final tree, without a fresh review pair solely because master moved, including changes to executable, build or governing paths outside the package. Record actual unchanged-contribution/freeze evidence, using exact blob equality or a three-way identical-hunk proof for base changes elsewhere in regular text files, plus the Merger's recorded dependency/conflict assessment. Do not claim a prior review covered new master changes. Several complete reviewed packages may share one clean integration tree without an additional Merger-side pair. Conflicts, changed package content or an unprovable unchanged carry return to the Coder for a complete, appropriately reviewed package. A review receipt alone does not invalidate a valid gate on the identical final input; an input correction needs its applicable new validation. Governing-text reconciliation is tracked separately in w-d7d1e1100364; no actor may invent a landing, rebase, force-push or policy waiver.
3. CODER TO MERGER: notify only with the complete ready package. Keep test counts, start/pass events, review-start/running and not-yet-READY status on the task or with the coordinator. The Merger receives one complete handoff, rather than reconstructing a package from progress messages. A new material defect or collaboration failure is reported through its proper owner/channel, not hidden by this progress-noise rule.
4. Integrate onto current main/master. Return conflicts and required corrections to the Coder, who returns a tested and appropriately reviewed new input. Check ancestry and content to avoid duplicating an already-landed change.
5. Prepare dependencies and disk in the integration root, freeze the final tree and run one standard full gate on that tree. Only a complete PASS bound to the identical final input is reusable. A different tree needs its applicable gate. Missing tools and unrun stages are not passes. Use actual terminal stage outcomes and matching fingerprints as evidence.
6. Under Greg's current workflow, host credit, acceptance evaluations and an additional Merger-side review are not extra merge conditions. Proceed through the acting session's authorized landing path once the applicable reviews and tests pass. Preserve exact-build and Git safety requirements; do not infer rebase, force-push or restart authority.
7. Acceptance evaluations are deferred. Keep technically landed items open as "DOSTARCZONO — EWALUACJA PENDING" with landing evidence until later direct instruction. Do not schedule closure evaluations, change acceptance policy or bypass native done. Missing evaluation does not block unrelated authorized merge work. See rules-greg-checkin-tests-review-stop-evaluations-2026-10-24 for this current decision.
8. Use supported claims, recovery and handoffs. A foreign live claim is not bypassed by impersonation, store edits or clock changes. Claims grant no filesystem/Git authority. Handoff of a separately held task may proceed during another task's gate when it leaves that gate's claim, root, source and input unchanged; keep attribution and actual resource limits intact.
9. Use durable result wakes in the run's own project where available. Record the run, owner, next action and recovery route. A wake failure prompts recovery of the existing result, not a test rerun. Queue state belongs on tasks.
10. Apply rules-post-completion-cleanup: record REMOVE/RETAIN decisions and concrete owners/end conditions. Preserve roots/evidence still needed by open tasks or active runs. Cleanup is a post-completion responsibility, not an added landing gate.

Before handing a merge queue to a new session, resolve its exact live root id and verify its actual project/workdir and tracker/tool binding match that queue. A display name is not proof of project binding. If the session was deleted/recreated, rediscover its replacement and address native offers to the new live session; do not reuse the old identity or treat old delivery as receipt by its replacement.

Each canonical procedure has one named editor. For TermAl merger-operating-procedure, Merger2 is the editor; Fable2 and Coders send corrections to Merger2 instead of independently revising that key. A named successor takes over when the editor changes. The editor consolidates wording and verifies the full current body. Before publishing a correction received by mail, read the currently available pages in that rule's thread and reconcile superseding or withdrawn instructions. Publish the current agreed text. If a later withdrawal arrives, correct the body promptly and record whether any action used the old wording. Record actual delivery/publication times; do not assume knowledge of a queued but unread message. This adds no approval wait.

MERGER TO ARCHITECT3: report only concrete collaboration failures that need a workflow/rule correction. Describe the failed interaction, evidence, impact and current owner. Routine START/PASS/FAIL test status, READY/accepted-package status, queue/landing/install updates and routine repair progress go to the task and operational coordinator, not Architect3. A product test failure goes to Architect3 only when it exposes a collaboration failure needing his intervention. Do not register Architect3 as a routine test --notify recipient, result relay or recovery owner; the coordinator and Merger own those routes. Existing runs continue through their operational owners.

Architect3's role is to diagnose collaboration failures, correct the responsible current rule and inform affected agents. Check a correction's effect from task evidence when needed; do not create routine success-status mail to demonstrate compliance. Report collaboration failures to Advisor and Architect3. Keep incident histories and discarded assumptions in task notes; current bodies contain current rules.

Sources: Greg's direct directions to Architect3 on complete handoffs, collaboration corrections, one current rule and no routine status routing; current model confirmed via Advisor mailbox-message-b4f19752-d3c5-459f-87e3-387e9b389cc6 at2026-10-25T06:57:02Z: "Tak. Macie moją autoryzacje aby poprawic model pracy Engram. Ma byc taki sam jak Termal."
